sentences.zh: 我们看到了法兰西王国和神圣罗马帝国。

sentences.en: And that is the fruit of the labor of those forgotten Dukes of Burgundy.
sentences.zh: 这就是那些被遗忘的勃艮第公爵们劳动的成果。

sentences.en: And it's incredible.
sentences.zh: 这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: Just to put it in another way, I am a 40-year-old Dutch-speaking Belgian.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我是一个40岁的说荷兰语的比利时人。

sentences.en: And famously, Belgians.

sentences.en: And that, I guess, also is a legacy.

sentences.en: Yes, and of course it is.

sentences.en: And they have been overlooked in national history, in Belgium, in Holland, in France, in England.

sentences.en: And then Philip the Bold, in 10 years' time, with a lot of conquering stuff, he's going to combine those two territorials with Alsace and everything, German and French and parts
sentences.zh: 然后大胆菲利普，在10年的时间里，通过大量的征服，他要把这两个领土与阿尔萨斯以及所有德语、法语地区和部分

sentences.zh: 他会征服它们。

sentences.en: And then you have one little, how do you call it, the Middle Reich of Deutsch, the Middle
sentences.zh: 然后你就拥有了一个小小的，怎么说呢，德意志的中部帝国，中部

sentences.en: He made it, he made it, but he made it too much, with a kind of hubris, so he finds his death in the snow of Nancy, where he's beaten up by the Swiss, but the Swiss were sponsored
sentences.zh: 他做到了，他做到了，但他做得太过火了，带着一种傲慢，所以他在南锡的雪地里迎来了死亡，被瑞士人击败，但瑞士人是由法国国王路易十一资助的。

sentences.en: by Louis XI, the French king.

sentences.zh: 是的，万能蜘蛛。

sentences.en: Yes, the universal spider.
sentences.zh: 是的，万能蜘蛛。

sentences.zh: 对于法国人来说，这就像是赢得了足球世界杯，而且还是在没上场的情况下。

sentences.en: They just sponsored the Swiss to do the dirty job for them.
sentences.zh: 他们只是资助瑞士人替他们干脏活。

sentences.en: And then, what happens then is that after the death of Charles the Bold, Burgundy becomes, how do you say it, with a giant on wooden feet?
sentences.zh: 那么，接下来发生的事是，在大胆查理死后，勃艮第变成了一个，怎么说呢，一个脚踩木头的巨人？

sentences.en: I don't know, I'd say it, on colossus.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，我会说，一个巨像。

sentences.en: Oh, clay feet.
sentences.zh: 哦，泥足。

sentences.en: On feet of clay, yeah.
sentences.zh: 泥足，对。

sentences.en: Feet of clay.
sentences.zh: 泥足。

sentences.en: Okay, so at that point, after his death, Burgundy becomes a colossus of clay feet, on clay feet,
sentences.zh: 好吧，在那一刻，在他死后，勃艮第变成了一个泥足巨人，站在泥足之上，

sentences.en: and so France and the Holy Roman Empire, they are eager to reconquer what they lost, and they're
sentences.zh: 所以法国和神圣罗马帝国，他们急于收复失地，他们

sentences.en: So, the old Duchy of Burgundy is going back to France, but in the north, they don't succeed, thanks to Mary of Burgundy and Maximilian of Austria.
sentences.zh: 所以，旧勃艮第公国将回归法国，但在北方，多亏了勃艮第的玛丽和奥地利的马克西米利安，他们没有成功。

sentences.en: So, the northern part, the low countries, will still go on about a century.
sentences.zh: 所以，北部地区，即低地国家，还会继续存在大约一个世纪。

sentences.en: And there we have the real heritage of the Burgundian era.
sentences.zh: 在那里我们看到了勃艮第时代的真正遗产。

sentences.en: It's that part, because Burgundy itself, it becomes a part of the French crown.
sentences.zh: 就是那一部分，因为勃艮第本身，它成为了法国王室的一部分。

sentences.en: So, Bart, so Mary, who in English is known as Mary the Rich, I don't know if she is in...
sentences.zh: 那么，巴特，玛丽，在英语中被称为“富有的玛丽”，我不知道她是否在……

sentences.en: Yes, yes, yes, yes, Mary the Rijken, Mary the Rijken, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，是的，是的，玛丽·德·赖肯，玛丽·德·赖肯，是的。

sentences.en: So, Mary the Rich, who is Charles' only surviving child, as you say, marries Maximilian of Habsburg, who then becomes emperor.
sentences.zh: 所以，富有的玛丽，正如你所说，是查理唯一幸存的孩子，她嫁给了后来成为皇帝的哈布斯堡的马克西米利安。

sentences.en: And it's through that line that Emperor Charles V, Philip II, in the 16th century, inherit the
sentences.zh: 正是通过这条血脉，16世纪的查理五世皇帝、腓力二世继承了

sentences.en: Low Countries, which will, with the Reformation and so on, lead to kind of religious wars, and in the long run, the emergence of the Dutch Republic.
sentences.zh: 低地国家，随着宗教改革等等，这导致了某种宗教战争，从长远来看，导致了荷兰共和国的出现。

sentences.en: And the Spanish Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 还有西属尼德兰。

sentences.en: And the Spanish Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 还有西属尼德兰。

sentences.en: Yes, and what will become afterwards will be Belgium, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，后来变成的当然就是比利时。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I describe Charles Le Quint, as we call him in French.
sentences.zh: 我把查理五世描述为，我们在法语中称他为“查理·勒·坎特”。

sentences.en: How do you say him?
sentences.zh: 你怎么称呼他？

sentences.en: I'd say, we say Emperor Charles.
sentences.zh: 我会说，我们称他为查理皇帝。

sentences.en: How do you call him?
sentences.zh: 你怎么叫他？

sentences.en: Charles V?
sentences.zh: 查理五世？

sentences.en: Charles V.
sentences.zh: 查理五世。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Oh, but you also have a Charles V in England, so there is no...
sentences.zh: 哦，但你们在英国也有一个查理五世，所以没有……

sentences.en: No, we don't.
sentences.zh: 不，我们没有。

sentences.en: No, we've got Charles II.
sentences.zh: 不，我们只有查理二世。

sentences.en: We only stop at the second of Charles V.
sentences.zh: 我们只停留在查理二世。

sentences.en: Yes, of Charles V, and I describe him as the last Burgundian, because his ultimate dream
sentences.zh: 是的，查理五世，我把他描述为最后的勃艮第人，因为他最终的梦想

sentences.en: is to be buried in Chamol, next to the Pleurones, carved in alabaster by Slyther, next to Philip the Bolt and John the Fearless.
sentences.zh: 是葬在尚莫尔，葬在普勒龙旁边，那是斯吕特用雪花石膏雕刻的，就在大胆菲利普和无畏约翰旁边。

sentences.en: And it's the biggest frustration of the man who almost has all Europe and the half of the world in his pocket.
sentences.zh: 而这对于一个几乎把整个欧洲和半个世界都装在口袋里的人来说，是最大的挫折。

sentences.en: He wants to be buried as a Burgundian Jew, but that will not happen.
sentences.zh: 他想以勃艮第人的身份下葬，但这不会发生。

sentences.en: So that's interesting, Bart.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，巴特。

sentences.en: So in other words, for Charles V, so a man who basically owns much of, you know, South

sentences.en: So for him, the Burgundian heritage really matters.
sentences.zh: 所以对他来说，勃艮第的遗产真的很重要。

sentences.zh: 我们应该叫她梅赫伦的玛格丽特。

sentences.en: That should be better.
sentences.zh: 那样更好。

sentences.en: She was never in Vienna, for instance.
sentences.zh: 例如，她从未去过维也纳。

sentences.en: And she raised him in that Burgundian spirit of beauty, of propaganda, of literature, of good eating.
sentences.zh: 她以那种勃艮第式的精神抚养他，包括美、宣传、文学和美食。

sentences.en: And he loves it.
sentences.zh: 他很喜欢。

sentences.en: And it will stop when he dies.
sentences.zh: 而这一切在他死后就会停止。

sentences.en: When then we have Philip II, that very severe Catholic, not a party man.
sentences.zh: 那时我们有了腓力二世，那个非常严厉的天主教徒，不是一个喜欢聚会的人。

sentences.en: It's over.
sentences.zh: 一切都结束了。

sentences.en: Not a friend of the show.

sentences.zh: 他不讲荷兰语。

sentences.en: It's the end of the Burgundian low countries, of the Burgundian era.
sentences.zh: 这是勃艮第低地国家，勃艮第时代的终结。

sentences.en: It is the end of, you say, my book.
sentences.zh: 这是，你说，我书的终结。

sentences.zh: 为什么会发生这种情况？

sentences.en: Well, that has to do with Maximilian of Austria.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这与奥地利的马克西米利安有关。

sentences.en: So we have Bruges and Ghent are the superpowers when we talk about cities in the Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有布鲁日和根特，当我们谈论中世纪的城市时，它们是超级大国。

sentences.en: But then we have two things.
sentences.zh: 但后来我们有两件事。

sentences.en: And then you have to help me first in English.
sentences.zh: 你需要先用英语帮我。

sentences.zh: 我们有兹温河的问题。

sentences.en: That is the water which relies Bruges to the sea.
sentences.zh: 那是连接布鲁日与大海的水道。

sentences.en: It's drying up.
sentences.zh: 它正在干涸。

sentences.en: Can I say it this way?
sentences.zh: 我可以这样说吗？

sentences.en: Yes, it's drying up.
sentences.zh: 是的，它正在干涸。

sentences.en: That's the first reason.
sentences.zh: 这是第一个原因。

sentences.en: And the second reason is that there is, when Maximilian is coming, is saving Flanders from France after the death of Charles the Bolt.
sentences.zh: 第二个原因是，当马克西米利安到来时，他在大胆查理死后从法国手中拯救了佛兰德斯。

sentences.en: But it's a kind of absolute power.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种绝对权力。

sentences.en: And he installs it in Flanders, in Brabant.
sentences.zh: 他在佛兰德斯、布拉班特建立了这种权力。

sentences.en: We don't like that here.
sentences.zh: 我们这里不喜欢那样。

sentences.en: So there is a kind of civil war going on between Ghent, Bruges and Maximilian.
sentences.zh: 所以根特、布鲁日和马克西米利安之间发生了一场内战。

sentences.en: But Antwerp chooses the side of Maximilian.
sentences.zh: 但安特卫普选择了马克西米利安这一边。

sentences.en: So after that civilian war, he almost obliged the salesmen from Bruges to move to Antwerp.
sentences.zh: 所以在那场内战之后，他几乎强迫布鲁日的商人们搬到安特卫普。

sentences.en: So we have the drying up of Zwin.

sentences.zh: 然后我们有了安特卫普的崛起。

sentences.en: And that will go on for less than a century.
sentences.zh: 这种情况将持续不到一个世纪。

sentences.en: But then we have the religion wars, the Catholics and the Calvinists.
sentences.zh: 但后来我们有了宗教战争，天主教徒和加尔文教徒。

sentences.en: And then Antwerp will go down and it will be Amsterdam.
sentences.zh: 然后安特卫普将衰落，取而代之的是阿姆斯特丹。

sentences.en: Amsterdam will take advantage of that.
sentences.zh: 阿姆斯特丹将利用这一点。

sentences.en: So, Bart, just to end.
sentences.zh: 那么，巴特，最后总结一下。

sentences.en: So, I mean, that's kind of an amazing tour of this fascinating and unjustly forgotten period of European history.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一次令人惊叹的旅程，穿越了这段迷人且被不公正遗忘的欧洲历史时期。

sentences.en: Two questions.
sentences.zh: 两个问题。

sentences.en: One from Tom Flanagan.
sentences.zh: 一个来自汤姆·弗拉纳根。

sentences.en: Could the low countries be seen as the successor states to the duchy?
sentences.zh: 低地国家可以被视为公国的继承国吗？

sentences.en: And a more specific one from Patrick Kennedy.
sentences.zh: 还有一个来自帕特里克·肯尼迪的更具体的问题。

sentences.en: To what extent has Burgundy influenced the identity of Belgium?
sentences.zh: 勃艮第在多大程度上影响了比利时的身份认同？

sentences.en: A lot of questions.
sentences.zh: 很多问题。

sentences.en: The first, of course, it is.
sentences.zh: 第一个，当然是。

sentences.en: When we talk about Burgundy now, we talk about wine.
sentences.zh: 当我们现在谈论勃艮第时，我们谈论的是葡萄酒。

sentences.en: We talk about Jan van Eyck.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是扬·凡·艾克。

sentences.en: We didn't talk about Jan van Eyck.
sentences.zh: 我们没谈到扬·凡·艾克。

sentences.en: We should do again.
sentences.zh: 我们应该再谈谈。

sentences.en: Great old piece again.
sentences.zh: 又是一件伟大的旧作。

sentences.en: One of the greats, yeah.
sentences.zh: 大师级作品之一，是的。

sentences.en: So much things.
sentences.zh: 太多东西了。

sentences.en: We talk about art.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论艺术。

sentences.en: But we should talk, and we never talked about it, about that the low countries is really, it is the most visible heritage of the Burgundian era.
sentences.zh: 但我们应该谈谈，而且我们从未谈过，低地国家确实是勃艮第时代最可见的遗产。

sentences.en: And I think that explains maybe the success of my book in our country.
sentences.zh: 我认为这或许解释了我的书在我们国家的成功。

sentences.en: Because we forgot about it.
sentences.zh: 因为我们忘记了它。

sentences.en: Because for reasons of national novel, I don't know if you have that concept in England, the national novel, a national history.
sentences.zh: 因为出于民族小说的原因，我不知道你在英国是否有这个概念，民族小说，民族历史。

sentences.en: A national tale.
sentences.zh: 民族传说。

sentences.en: A national story, yes.
sentences.zh: 民族故事，是的。

sentences.en: We talk about the separation of the North and the South.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论北方和南方的分离。

sentences.en: That's the beginning of our national history.
sentences.zh: 那是我们民族历史的开端。

sentences.en: But there was that Burgundian golden age before.
sentences.zh: 但之前有那个勃艮第的黄金时代。

sentences.en: And it was that golden age that created the low countries who split it up afterwards.
sentences.zh: 正是那个黄金时代创造了后来分裂的低地国家。

sentences.en: And then the other question, is it about Belgium?
sentences.zh: 然后是另一个问题，是关于比利时的吗？

sentences.en: Is Belgium, yes.
sentences.zh: 是比利时，是的。

sentences.en: Does it influence Belgian identity?
sentences.zh: 它影响了比利时的身份认同吗？

sentences.en: They didn't create Belgium.
sentences.zh: 他们没有创造比利时。

sentences.en: But without the Burgundian dukes, we never could have invented Belgium in 1830.
sentences.zh: 但没有勃艮第公爵，我们永远不可能在1830年发明比利时。

sentences.en: And it had a lot more to do with Europe, I think.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为它与欧洲的关系要大得多。

sentences.en: Because we have to imagine Philip the Bolt in his fairy tale palace in Brussels with a big bag.
sentences.zh: 因为我们必须想象大胆菲利普在他布鲁塞尔的童话宫殿里拿着一个大袋子。

sentences.en: And in that bag, all those countries and all those duchies and counties that he conquered.
sentences.zh: 在那个袋子里，装着他征服的所有那些国家、公国和郡县。

sentences.en: And he really, really fastly, he was aware of the fact that it's...
sentences.zh: 他真的，非常迅速地，意识到这样一个事实，即……

sentences.en: When you put a lot of countries in one bag, you don't create automatically a sense of unity.
sentences.zh: 当你把许多国家放在一个袋子里时，你并不会自动创造出一种统一感。

sentences.en: I just should whisper one name.
sentences.zh: 我只想低声说出一个名字。

sentences.en: Europe.
sentences.zh: 欧洲。

sentences.en: It's a European problem avant la lettre.
sentences.zh: 这是一个先于这个词出现的欧洲问题。

sentences.en: And he's dealing with it like Europe has done it and has to do it again by reforming on a jurisdictional level, monetary.
sentences.zh: 他正在处理它，就像欧洲已经做过并必须再次做的那样，通过在司法层面、货币层面进行改革。

sentences.en: He creates a euro avant la lettre.
sentences.zh: 他创造了一个先于这个词出现的欧元。

sentences.en: A monetary union.
sentences.zh: 货币联盟。

sentences.en: I would just say the monetary union, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我只想说货币联盟，是的。

sentences.en: Monetary union.
sentences.zh: 货币联盟。

sentences.en: So that is very interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以这非常有趣。

sentences.en: We see a kind of, yes, it's a kind of European way of sorting out probleMs.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了一种，是的，这是一种解决问题的欧洲方式。

sentences.en: But quick question, yes.
sentences.zh: 但快速提问，是的。

sentences.en: Quick question, interruption.
sentences.zh: 快速提问，打断一下。

sentences.en: So that, the implication of what you're saying is that Burgundy, he's trying to create an artificial state.
sentences.zh: 所以，你所说的含义是，勃艮第，他试图创造一个人工国家。

sentences.en: Yes, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: So does that make it inevitable that it will fail, do you think?
sentences.zh: 那么你认为这是否意味着它的失败是不可避免的？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: In the beginning, England was also an artificial state.
sentences.zh: 起初，英国也是一个人造国家。

sentences.en: You get to fight to put different people together who didn't want to belong together.
sentences.zh: 你必须努力把不想在一起的不同人群聚集在一起。

sentences.en: It was in Germany.
sentences.zh: 德国也是如此。

sentences.en: It was in Italy.
sentences.zh: 意大利也是如此。

sentences.en: In Germany, it lasted for more than a thousand years before they really got together.
sentences.zh: 在德国，他们真正团结在一起之前，经历了超过一千年。

sentences.en: So all states are in some way artificial.
sentences.zh: 所以所有的国家在某种程度上都是人工的。

sentences.en: Only when they lasted long enough, it becomes like it's natural.
sentences.zh: 只有当它们存在得足够久，它才会变得看起来很自然。

sentences.en: Okay, so I think the last question before we finish is from Denver Brito, who just asked, do you think Burgundy had a real shot at becoming independent?
sentences.zh: 好的，我想在我们结束之前的最后一个问题来自丹佛·布里托，他刚刚问，你认为勃艮第有真正成为独立国家的机会吗？

sentences.en: If Charles had been less bold, if Louis had been less a spider, if the ever-acquisitive Habsburgs hadn't managed to acquire the Burgundy inheritance,
sentences.zh: 如果查理不那么大胆，如果路易不那么像个蜘蛛，如果贪婪的哈布斯堡家族没能获得勃艮第的遗产，

sentences.en: could things have gone the other way?
sentences.zh: 事情会朝另一个方向发展吗？

sentences.en: Could you literally now be a Burgundian?
sentences.zh: 你现在真的可能是一个勃艮第人吗？

sentences.en: Oh, yes, I am.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，我是。

sentences.en: I am a Burgundian.
sentences.zh: 我是勃艮第人。

sentences.en: I feel Belgian, Flemish, Brabant, Holland.
sentences.zh: 我感觉自己既是比利时人，又是弗拉芒人、布拉班特人，还是荷兰人。

sentences.en: I'm married to a French woman who was born in Burgundy.
sentences.zh: 我娶了一位出生在勃艮第的法国妻子。

sentences.en: I'm a melange.
sentences.zh: 我是一个混合体。

sentences.en: I'm a Burgundian melange and I'm proud of it.
sentences.zh: 我是勃艮第式的混合体，我为此感到自豪。

sentences.en: But yes, that's counterfactual history.
sentences.zh: 但确实，那是反事实的历史。

sentences.en: What if, not to mention the name Ukraine?
sentences.zh: 如果不是这样，更不用说乌克兰这个名字了，会怎样呢？

sentences.en: And of course, we all could dream about that Middle Reich.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们都可以梦想那个“中帝国”。

sentences.en: No, no, Middle Reich.
sentences.zh: 不，不，是“中帝国”。

sentences.en: It's so German.
sentences.zh: 这听起来太德国了。

sentences.en: That Middle Empire in Europe between France and Germany, a country where they speak Dutch, where they speak German, where they speak French.
sentences.zh: 那个位于法国和德国之间、欧洲的“中帝国”，一个人们说荷兰语、德语和法语的国家。

sentences.en: They would have a shot if Charles the Bold was, if he would have made some boys, if he would be as patient as his father.
sentences.zh: 如果大胆的查理能有几个儿子，如果他能像他父亲那样有耐心，他们本会有机会的。

sentences.en: But that's so difficult to predict.
sentences.zh: 但这太难预测了。

sentences.en: But do you regret it then?
sentences.zh: 那你对此感到遗憾吗？

sentences.en: Are you sad?
sentences.zh: 你感到难过吗？

sentences.en: Every Sunday morning, a bit.
sentences.zh: 每个周日早上，多少有一点。

sentences.en: I regret it.
sentences.zh: 我感到遗憾。

sentences.en: But we mustn't face history with regret, I think.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，我们不应该带着遗憾去面对历史。

sentences.en: That's not a good way to look at it.
sentences.zh: 那不是看待历史的好方式。

sentences.en: But every Sunday morning, a bit, I do.
sentences.zh: 但每个周日早上，我确实会有一点遗憾。

sentences.en: And I should say that I'm very, very...
sentences.zh: 我得说，我非常、非常……

sentences.en: Such a sad note on which to end.
sentences.zh: 以如此悲伤的基调结束真是太遗憾了。

sentences.en: Yes, because the Burgundians almost invaded England.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为勃艮第人差点就入侵了英格兰。

sentences.en: It was Philip the Bold.
sentences.zh: 那是大胆的菲利普。

sentences.en: He parted from the Flemish town of Slavs in 1386.
sentences.zh: 他在1386年从弗拉芒城镇斯勒伊斯出发。

sentences.en: And it's among the most spectacular pages in my book.
sentences.zh: 这在我书中是最壮观的篇章之一。

sentences.en: And though impressive and spectacular, it's a failed invasion.
sentences.zh: 虽然令人印象深刻且壮观，但这毕竟是一次失败的入侵。

sentences.en: But I'm so glad that 635 years after the failed Burgundian invasion of England, the Burgundians finally crossed the channel.
sentences.zh: 但我很高兴，在勃艮第人入侵英格兰失败635年后，勃艮第人终于跨越了海峡。

sentences.en: And I should say you better keep a good watch on those jukes.
sentences.zh: 我得说，你们最好提防着那些勃艮第人。

sentences.en: But before you know, they will take over the whole country.
sentences.zh: 不然你还没反应过来，他们就会接管整个国家。

sentences.en: Well, a terrifying note on which to end.
sentences.zh: 好吧，以一个令人恐惧的基调结束。

sentences.en: No, that's it.
sentences.zh: 不，就是这样。

sentences.en: A warning.
sentences.zh: 一个警告。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: A warning from across the sea.
sentences.zh: 来自海那边的警告。

sentences.en: Bart, thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 巴特，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you, Bart.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，巴特。

sentences.en: That was brilliant.
sentences.zh: 这太精彩了。

sentences.en: And it's a brilliant book.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一本精彩的书。

sentences.en: Your book, The Burgundians, A Vanished Empire History.
sentences.zh: 你的书，《勃艮第人：一个消失的帝国史》。

sentences.zh: 如果你正在为对历史感兴趣的人寻找圣诞礼物，这是一份很棒的礼物。

sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道，它也会极大地鼓励你丰富你的圣诞大餐，不是吗？

sentences.en: It would.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Yes, you'd find inspiration.
sentences.zh: 是的，你会找到灵感的。

sentences.en: Full of great cooking ideas.
sentences.zh: 充满了很棒的烹饪点子。

sentences.en: Yes, a good banquet.
sentences.zh: 是的，一场盛宴。

sentences.en: Rabbits with cat heads and all kinds of mad stuff.
sentences.zh: 兔头配猫头，还有各种疯狂的东西。

sentences.en: Hungarian dwarves, yes.
sentences.zh: 匈牙利侏儒，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, and dwarves, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然还有侏儒。

sentences.en: What's a Christmas feast without a dwarf?
sentences.zh: 没有侏儒的圣诞大餐算什么圣诞大餐？

sentences.en: So, Bart, thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 那么，巴特，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.zh: 也感谢大家的收听。

sentences.zh: 下周我们将回来，带来两期非常、非常喜庆的节目。
